name: Chess Pie

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to the lowest position and preheat oven to 220°C (425°F). Lightly prick chilled pie shell all over bottom in 1.5-cm intervals. Line pie shell with a double layer 36-cm square of parchment paper or aluminum foil. Fill with sugar, pie weights, or dried beans.

Transfer to a parchment or foil-lined rimmed baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes. Reduce oven temperature to 160°C (325°F). Carefully remove liner and pie weights from crust and continue to bake until the crust is cooked through and just starting to turn golden brown, 5 to 8 minutes. Set aside and let cool completely, about 30 minutes.

In a large bowl, whisk eggs, butter, milk, and vanilla together until smooth. Pour sugar into the egg mixture in a slow steady stream, whisking as you go until well combined. Whisk cornmeal, flour, vinegar, and salt into the mixture until smooth.

Pour the filling into the parbaked pie shell. Bake until the filling is lightly browned and center of the pie is just set, but still jiggles slightly when shaken, and register 180℉(82℃), 45 to 50 minutes. If necessary, shield edges of crust with aluminum foil to prevent overbrowning. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool completely, about 4 hours. Slice and serve.

description: This is a great, basic recipe for Chess Pie, the gooey, sweet Southern classic. The sweet, rich custard filling is balanced with a touch of white vinegar. A small amount of flour and cornmeal create its signature thin, crispy caramelized crust.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 5 hr 45 min.

Make-ahead and storage: Pie can be refrigerated for up to 4 days. The pie can be served chilled or at room temperature.
author: Lauren Weisenthal
